# No proposal without an identified decision maker

`sales.rule.core.no_proposal_without_decision_maker` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core** · kind **rule**

> Withhold a priced proposal until the person who can release the money is named, and either met or booked. A proposal issued below that line is not a sales artefact — it is a free benchmarking document the buyer uses to negotiate with someone else.


## The rule

**A priced proposal is not issued while the economic buyer — the individual who can approve the spend without asking anyone else — is unnamed, or is named but has never been met and has no meeting booked. The gate is the person, not the title, and not the champion's assurance that they will "take it upstairs".
**


Spans `sales.obj.core.proposal`, `sales.obj.core.decision_maker`, `sales.obj.core.buying_committee`, `sales.obj.core.deal` · severity **blocking** · enforced by `L5_validation`


When: `has_obs: proposal_sent` AND `no_obs: introduction` AND `edge_count <= 3` AND `deal.status = open`


_Why:_ Price is the only irreversible disclosure in a sales cycle. Once a number is in the buyer's inbox it is in the procurement file, the competitor's negotiation, and next year's renewal conversation, and it can never be raised — only defended. Giving it to someone with no authority buys nothing in return, because a non-buyer cannot say yes and therefore cannot trade anything for it. Worse, the proposal ends the discovery: the champion now has a document to circulate, so the seller loses the reason to ask for the meeting that would have identified the approver in the first place.



## Failure modes

- Title substitution. A VP of Operations is recorded as the decision maker because the title sounds senior, the gate opens, and the proposal goes to someone whose signing limit is a tenth of the deal. Authority is a spend limit, not a job title.
- Champion laundering. The champion says 'I'll get it approved', that is logged as approver access, and the rule is satisfied by a sentence in an email. A champion who has never arranged a meeting with the buyer is a preference, not a path.
- Compliance theatre — a fifteen-minute introductory call with the buyer booked purely to clear the gate, with no agenda the buyer values. It satisfies the check and teaches the buyer that the seller wastes their time, which is a more expensive outcome than the delay.
- Applying it to a one-page pricing indication in a transactional deal, where the eight-day cycle makes the gate cost more than the leak it prevents.


## Limits

- edge_count is a proxy for coverage, not for authority. A deal with eleven contacts and no approver among them passes the machine test and fails the rule. L4 must confirm against the Decision Maker object; the predicate only surfaces candidates for that check.
- In organisations that buy by committee consensus — most of European mid-market, most of Japan — there is no single economic buyer to identify, and insisting on one produces a fabricated name in the CRM. There the rule reads: the approval ROUTE is documented and every seat on it is accounted for.
- The rule says nothing about timing beyond ordering. A proposal correctly issued to the right person at the wrong moment — before the pain is quantified — fails for a different reason this rule cannot see.


## Variants by model or offering

| Applies to | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `sales.model.enterprise_sales` | Raise the bar from 'met' to 'the economic buyer has stated the business outcome in their own words, in a meeting the seller attended'.  | At enterprise deal sizes the approver's own articulation of value is the only thing that survives contact with procurement, because procurement's job is to attack the seller's articulation of it.  |
| `sales.model.smb_sales` | Collapse to a single test: is the person on the call the owner or the budget holder? | In a company of thirty people the buyer, champion and user are usually the same person, and a multi-step gate adds days to a cycle that is measured in days.  |
| `sales.model.plg` | Defer the gate to the expansion boundary. Self-serve and team-tier purchases are made on a company card by the user; the rule engages when a deal crosses into an annual contract or a security review.  | Product-led motions deliberately sell below the approval line, and the whole strategy is to arrive at the economic buyer with usage already inside the building.  |
| `sales.model.government_sales` | Replace 'economic buyer' with 'the funded programme and its contracting officer'. The approver is a budget line and a procurement vehicle, and both are matters of public record.  | Public bodies separate the person who wants the thing from the person who may buy it by statute. Identifying an enthusiastic official proves nothing about appropriated funds.  |
| `sales.offering.service` | Add the delivery sponsor to the gate — the person who will own the outcome after signature and whose team must be freed up for it.  | In services a large share of revenue depends on work done after signature, so an approver who has not committed the client-side resource has approved a project that cannot start.  |
